claims.text: Rapid quenching after high-temperature processing yields a random, disordered atomic distribution with minimal short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing HfNbTaTiZr within 600–900 °C promotes the formation of short-range chemical order.
Elevated-temperature annealing enables limited atomic diffusion that creates short-range chemical order.
Short-range chemical order alters dislocation pinning in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in dislocation pinning caused by short-range order modify the alloy's stress–strain behavior and yield strength.
Short-range chemical order affects lattice vibrations and lattice anharmonicity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The SRO-induced change in lattice dynamics modifies the elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr.
The SRO-induced change in lattice anharmonicity modifies the thermal expansion coefficient of HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealed samples containing SRO will exhibit a measurable yield-strength difference relative to rapidly quenched samples.
Annealed samples containing SRO will exhibit a measurable elastic-modulus difference relative to rapidly quenched samples.
Annealed samples containing SRO will exhibit a reduced or otherwise anomalously modified thermal expansion coefficient relative to rapidly quenched samples.
The proposed SRO-mediated relationships apply within the 600–900 °C test range.
Outside 600–900 °C, phase transformations or extensive grain growth may obscure the effects attributed to SRO.
X-ray diffraction or transmission electron microscopy can reveal signatures of SRO through features such as diffraction-peak modifications or diffuse scattering.
